Tf-idf features from texts

Source: R/core-bench-baseline.R
hr_tfidf.Rd

Turns texts into an l2-normalised tf-idf matrix, the feature set the baselines hr_baseline_classifier() and hr_baseline_ranker() use.

Usage

hr_tfidf(texts, min_df = 2, max_features = 5000)

Arguments

texts

Character vector of texts. NA is read as an empty text.

min_df

Smallest number of texts a term must appear in.

max_features

Largest number of terms kept.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per text (named by names(texts) when present) and one column per term, in C-locale order. The idf weights are attached as the named vector attr(, "idf").

Details

  • Tokens are runs of letters and digits after lower-casing ("COVID-19" gives "covid" and "19"). There is no stemming and no stop word list.

  • A term is kept when it appears in at least min_df texts. If more than max_features terms pass, the most frequent across all texts are kept.

  • The weight of term j in text i is tf(i, j) * idf(j), where tf is the raw count and idf(j) = log((1 + n) / (1 + df(j))) + 1, with n texts and df(j) the number of texts containing j. This is the smoothed idf of scikit-learn's TfidfVectorizer, which ASReview uses.

  • Each row is then divided by its Euclidean norm. A text with no kept term is a row of zeros.

The result is an ordinary dense base R matrix. That is fine at the sizes a benchmark reference or a screening set has (a few thousand texts by at most max_features terms is tens of megabytes); it is not meant for a corpus of millions.

References

Salton, G. and Buckley, C. (1988). Term-weighting approaches in automatic text retrieval. Information Processing and Management 24(5), 513-523.

Pedregosa, F. et al. (2011). Scikit-learn: machine learning in Python. Journal of Machine Learning Research 12, 2825-2830.

See also

Other baselines: hr_baseline_classifier(), hr_baseline_ranker()

Examples

m <- hr_tfidf(c("Masks cut infection.", "Masks and handwashing.",
                "Handwashing cut infection."))
round(m, 3)
#>        cut handwashing infection masks
#> [1,] 0.577       0.000     0.577 0.577
#> [2,] 0.000       0.707     0.000 0.707
#> [3,] 0.577       0.577     0.577 0.000
#> attr(,"idf")
#>         cut handwashing   infection       masks 
#>    1.287682    1.287682    1.287682    1.287682 
attr(m, "idf")
#>         cut handwashing   infection       masks 
#>    1.287682    1.287682    1.287682    1.287682
